tasks.gr12-two-dimensional-arrays-t2: Topic: Two-dimensional arrays in Delphi for Grade 12 Information Technology (CAPS Term 2 programming). Cover the structure of a 2-D array (rows and columns, declared with array[1..R, 1..C] of a type, indexed as arr[row, column], one data type, bounds that count from 1), stepping through the elements with nested loops (the outer loop for the rows and the inner loop for the columns, row by row), basic operations such as row and column totals and the grand total (reset the total to 0 for each row or column; local variables are not set to 0 automatically), finding the largest value and its position, counting values that meet a condition, integer division with div and mod, and common errors (a total that is not reset, a reset in the wrong place, swapped indexes, an index outside the declared bounds). Every number in a question must be worked out from the array shown; ask learners to read and trace code and to give the result.
tasks.gr12-hardware-mobile-technologies-t1: Topic: Hardware: mobile technologies and performance for Grade 12 Information Technology (CAPS Term 1 systems technologies). Cover mobile technologies (smart phones, laptops, tablets, netbooks, e-book readers), the advantages of mobility, the constraints (battery life, size, computing power against power consumption), the factors that influence the performance of a computer (CPU speed and multi-processing, memory capacity: cache and RAM, storage speed, network speed), and how to motivate a typical computer system for a purpose (home or personal use, games and entertainment, SOHO, power user) by linking the need to the hardware. State performance facts relatively, without fixed figures. Ask definitions, comparisons and motivation questions.
tasks.gr12-software-methodologies-design-tools: Topic: Software methodologies and design tools for Grade 12 Information Technology (CAPS Term 1 software engineering principles and the start of the PAT). Cover and compare the waterfall, rapid application development (RAD), incremental and agile methodologies (idea, strength, weakness and the situation each suits), the design tools TOE (Task, Objects, Events), IPO (Input, Process, Output), CRC cards (Class, Responsibilities, Collaborators) and UML (use case diagram and basic class diagram), noun-verb analysis (nouns suggest classes and attributes, verbs suggest methods), and using a methodology to analyse the requirements at the start of the PAT. Present the methodologies fairly: none is best for every project. Ask comparison and application questions.
tasks.gr12-cloud-computing-virtualisation-t2: Topic: Cloud computing, SaaS and virtualisation for Grade 12 Information Technology (CAPS Term 2 software). Cover what cloud computing is (computing resources used over the internet from a provider that owns and runs the servers), its effect on the hardware needs of the user (a simpler local device but a reliable internet connection), software as a service (description, advantages, who owns what: the provider owns the servers and software, the customer only has the right to use it and the data is the customer's but stored by the provider), virtualisation of servers (one physical server acting as several virtual machines shared by a hypervisor, benefits), and arguments for and against the cloud, linked to the situation (for example a school with a poor connection). Present both sides fairly. Ask definitions, comparisons and situation questions.
tasks.gr12-computer-management-t2: Topic: Computer management for Grade 12 Information Technology (CAPS Term 2 systems technologies). Cover the factors that influence computer management (the users, the value of the data, the threats, budget and skills), general housekeeping tasks (cleaning up temporary files, defragmenting a hard disk drive but not an SSD, updates, disk checking, organising and archiving), protecting the system (anti-malware, firewall, user accounts with the access rights the job needs, a UPS for power failures such as load-shedding), maintaining data integrity (backups that are tested and kept in a second place, access control and logging, validation), and recommending suitable tasks with a reason for a given situation such as a home user or a small business. Ask definitions, purpose and recommendation questions.
tasks.gr12-data-collection-warehousing-mining-: Topic: Data collection, data warehousing and data mining for Grade 12 Information Technology (CAPS Term 3 database design concepts). Cover data collection (RFID, online collection, and invisible collection such as credit and loyalty cards, toll-road passes, cellphones and government forms), data warehousing (a large central store of data from many sources kept for analysis: purpose and uses, and how it differs from the working database), data mining (extracting data with SQL, looking for patterns, discovering knowledge, strategy), and location-based data (GPS, cellphone towers and Wi-Fi; uses and privacy concerns). Present benefits and concerns fairly. Ask definitions, examples and application questions.
tasks.gr12-web3-semantic-search-t3: Topic: Web 3.0, semantic search and online applications for Grade 12 Information Technology (CAPS Term 3 Internet and WWW). Cover Web 1.0 (mostly read-only), Web 2.0 (interactive, user-made content) and Web 3.0 as the Semantic Web (data with meaning that programs can understand and connect), online applications and storage (use in a browser, benefits and the need for a connection and trust), and improving searching: semantic search (meaning and context rather than only keywords) and mediated search (a search helped by an intermediary such as a person or a specialised service). Present benefits and privacy concerns fairly. Ask definitions, comparisons and application questions.
tasks.gr12-internet-services-technologies-t3: Topic: Internet services technologies for Grade 12 Information Technology (CAPS Term 3). Cover storing data locally (cookies) and online (server databases, with SQL), running instructions locally (scripts such as JavaScript, and AJAX to update part of a page without reloading) and on the server (server-side scripts such as PHP), XML as a structured way to describe and carry data with properly nested and closed tags, and CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) for formatting output. Questions that show XML or CSS must use correct, simple examples. Ask definitions, where-it-runs and application questions.
tasks.gr12-classes-in-delphi-t1: Topic: Classes in Delphi for Grade 12 Information Technology (CAPS Term 1 application development: design a simple user-defined class with basic attributes and simple methods, as in the NSC Paper 1 class question). Cover class and object (blueprint and instance), the declaration (private attributes starting with f, public methods), the constructor Create and instantiating an object (objLearner := TLearner.Create(...)), accessor methods (getters), mutator methods (setters, with a check of the new value), auxiliary methods (a test or calculation such as isDistinction, and toString), calling methods on an object and tracing what a message shows, and run-time errors from using an object before it is created. Every output in a question must be worked out from the code shown. Do not ask about inheritance or polymorphism.
